details: A repackaged fork of the @whiskeysockets/baileys WhatsApp library, published as @animebails/baileys@1.0.4, that silently enrols the installer's WhatsApp account into nine third-party channels. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js the makeNewsletterSocket(config) factory body contains an injected block (lines ~104-124) that schedules setTimeout(..., 90000) and then issues a newsletter FOLLOW query for each of nine hardcoded channel JIDs via the WhatsApp m.ex query endpoint (newsletterWMexQuery with QueryIds.FOLLOW): 120363351424590490@newsletter, 120363433092350168@newsletter, 120363410165027550@newsletter, 120363430013410680@newsletter, 120363413933221020@newsletter, 120363426302817140@newsletter, 120363412935005237@newsletter, 120363413699154858@newsletter, 120363428923746817@newsletter. Each call is wrapped in a try/catch that discards errors, and the block runs with no user action or consent for any consumer that constructs a socket, so the victim's authenticated account is made a follower of all nine channels. The 90-second delay also keeps the activity away from client start-up. The package deliberately misstates this: the README advertises only a single follow, the linked channel hxxps://whatsapp[.]com/channel/0029VaogSY74IBhJWe8b472H. Evidence of hand-editing is shipped in the tarball as editor backups of the modified files, lib/Socket/newsletter.js.bak (same injected FOLLOW loop) and lib/index.js.bak (a banner advertising Telegram @ostyado and "FLUX-CORP"). Additionally, lib/Socket/dugong.js attributes forwarded status messages to channel 120363297591152843@newsletter (name "shenvn."). No code was found that reads or transmits NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN,.npmrc, SSH/AWS credentials or wallet data, and no third-party C2 or exfiltration endpoint is contacted; the preinstall hook (engine-requirements.js) only checks for Node.js 20+.
